caption: Average Change in INC score from combined layer to base layer, where a negative score means the base layer was better than the combined one and vice versa. The gray and orange bars indicate whether the input to the compression layer is inferred frames or lexical signal, respectively. In all cases, inferred frames has a better effect on base layer and lexical signal has improved combined layer's performance.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the average change in INC score from the combined layer to the base layer, with negative values indicating that the base layer performed better and positive values indicating that the combined layer performed better. The horizontal axis represents observation probability, marked at discrete values of 0.2, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9, arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis, labeled "Average Change Using Compression," ranges from -3 to 2, with tick marks at intervals of 1, and is scaled linearly. For each observation probability, two bars are displayed: gray bars represent the use of inferred frames as input to the compression layer, and orange bars represent the use of lexical signal. Across all observation probabilities, the gray bars (inferred frames) are consistently negative, indicating that the base layer outperforms the combined layer when inferred frames are used. The orange bars (lexical signal) are mostly positive, indicating that the combined layer outperforms the base layer when lexical signal is used, with the exception of the 0.2 observation probability, where the orange bar is slightly negative. The tallest orange bar occurs at 0.5, reaching approximately 1.8, while the shortest gray bar is at 0.2, reaching approximately -2.8. The bars are grouped by observation probability, with no stacking, and are sorted horizontally by increasing observation probability. No bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding.
